title: Candela scratch: finalist evaluation — Mira Lin
body:
Notes / quick scratch for myself + Arielle — trying to capture gut + evidence before I forget. Mira Lin interview (final loop) — senior runtime engineer candidate. Short timeline: phone screen 2025-01-15, take-home pair 2025-01-22, onsite loop 2025-02-02. Loop: 4 interviews (system design, runtime internals, debugging/oncall, culture/collaboration).

-- Immediate gut 
- Very calm and deliberate. Not flashy, focused on trade-offs.
- Repeatedly steered answers to cost/latency tradeoffs rather than purely feature design — aligns with Redwood value of production-first.
- Comfortable with kernel-level reasoning and also able to translate to product constraints.

-- Highlights from interviews 
1) System design (Arielle): Mira sketched a multi-tenant batching design that accounted for head-of-line blocking, KV cache eviction interactions, and burst capacity. Called out three real failure modes and mitigation (fairness queueing, per-tenant soft-quotas, degraded-mode fallbacks). Asked about metrics to monitor (p50/p95 latency by tenant, cache hit rate, per-tenant token-cost).
2) Runtime internals (Diego): Good explanation of attention cache memory management. Proposed a small modification to our KV cache snapshot format to make checkpoint/reload cheaper (delta checkpoints) — plausible and low-risk. Competent with quantization/dequant flow tradeoffs; asked about our compilation pipeline.
3) Debugging/oncall: Gave concrete postmortem example from current company — a misrouted config causing silent tokenization mismatch. Sound blameless analysis, owned remediation (deploy-safety gates + canary metric). Also sketched runbook for high latency: layered checks (hardware, kernel, model variant routing, batching saturation).
4) Collaboration/culture: Several examples of pushing change with low friction: small PRs + feature flags + docs, and working across infra/product. Comfortable pairing and code review.

-- Concrete evidence vs heuristics 
Strengths (evidence):
- Delta checkpoint idea came with rough complexity and rollback plan (evidence of practical engineering).
- Presented monitoring matrix — p50/p95/p99 per-tenant + cost buckets + cache hit. Able to prioritize which to instrument first.
- Oncall PM: had a concrete runbook example and owned a postmortem.

Weaknesses / Questions (evidence):
- Didn't show deep ownership of compiler/kernels (less hands-on in JIT/kernels at scale). Said "I've read the kernel codebase before" but not "I've authored kernels". Could ramp into this but needs mentorship.
- Some answers assumed linux perf tooling familiarity but less about GPU perf counters specifics (nvprof/rdpmc usage was vague).

-- Role scorecard (quick numbers, 1..5, write rationale)
- Runtime architecture: 4 — clear pattern library knowledge; solid trade-offs; missing 1 point for kernel-level authorship.
- Observability & SLOs: 5 — crisp monitoring-first answers, prioritized metrics.
- Oncall/crisis handling: 4 — owned PM and remediation; would like stronger example of large-scale incident ownership (company size difference?).
- Collaboration & writing: 5 — good; examples of docs + small PRs.
- Kernel/compiler depth: 3 — junior relative to our kernel experts; enough to contribute but not immediate author of custom kernels.

Aggregate (rough): 4.2/5 -> Strong hire for senior runtime engineer with mentorship on kernel teams.

-- Risk map (quick):
- Oncall stretch: moderate (could need help on GPU counters and low-level performance debugging early).
- Ramp time to deeply own compile/kernels: estimate 3–6 months with shadowing.
- Cultural fit: positive; low friction.

-- Suggested hiring decision & conditions 
- Recommend: hire (strong-yes).
- Conditions: pair with kernel lead for first 3 months, rotate through a dedicated infra oncall with buddy for first 30 days, include an explicit kernel learning plan in 90-day goals (readings + two kernel-modding PRs).

-- Suggested interview follow-ups / notes for offer packet 
- Compensation note: candidate currently on RSU-heavy comp; expect counteroffer window.
- Team placement: serving-runtime (batching & runtime infra) with close alignment to compiler/kernels team.
- Manager note: enjoys small deliverables + product-coupling; good candidate for features that require product tradeoff thinking.

-- TODOs for me before we send recommendation 
- Pull the take-home pair recording and timestamp the delta-checkpoint idea (evidence for hiring packet). Link: PR#4893 (Diego pair).
- Confirm references: asked for 2 — reach out to ex-manager (S. Turner) and peer (L. Gomez).
- Draft 90-day goals (kernel ramp + observability ownership) and share with hiring committee.

-- Raw snippets (quick copy-paste from my notes) 
"If we TTL the KV cache too aggressively we see tail-latency spikes due to cache churn; prefer tenant-aware TTL + background reclaim."
"Delta checkpoint: store small diff per change, compose on restore — reduces checkpoint window for big models; requires idempotent replay and version tags."

-- Off-the-cuff impression for panel:
- Bring Mira on. She'll be a stable senior engineer who improves our SLO thinking and runtime architecture. Expect 8–12 week ramp on kernels. Low risk on collaboration.

--- end scratch ---

History: I keep this in users because it's a pre-offer personal synthesis. Will move to shared_drives/company/hiring if we decide to make public or include in candidate packet.
